title: FutureHouse Robin Multi-Agent AI Scientist Discovers & Validates Ripasudil for Dry AMD
aiSystem: Robin (Crow, Falcon & Finch Multi-Agent System — FutureHouse)
whyItMatters: First open-source multi-agent AI scientist published in Nature to autonomously generate hypotheses, design wet-lab assays, analyze experimental data, and validate a novel therapeutic candidate (ripasudil) for dry AMD.
summary: Published in Nature in May 2026 (following a May 2025 preprint) by Ali Essam Ghareeb, Benjamin Chang, Ludovico Mitchener, Andrew D. White, and Samuel G. Rodriques at FutureHouse and the University of Oxford, Robin orchestrates specialized literature-search (Crow, Falcon) and data-analysis (Finch) agents in an iterative discovery loop. Tasked with finding treatments for dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD)—a leading cause of blindness—Robin synthesized 551 papers in 30 minutes, hypothesized enhancing retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) phagocytosis, proposed and iterated wet-lab experiments with human biologists, analyzed RNA-seq and flow-cytometry readouts, and identified the glaucoma ROCK inhibitor ripasudil as a validated therapeutic candidate.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously integrated literature synthesis (Crow & Falcon) with executable bioinformatics/assay data analysis (Finch) across multiple iterative experimental cycles.

Proposed increasing RPE phagocytosis as a novel dAMD therapeutic strategy, selected ripasudil (never previously proposed for dAMD), and interpreted follow-up RNA-seq data linking the effect to ABCA1 upregulation.
Released fully open-source under Apache-2.0 and published in Nature (655: 497–505) alongside Google’s AI Co-Scientist, demonstrating ~200× literature-synthesis speedup.
caveats: Physical pipetting, cell-culture assays, and experimental execution were performed by human laboratory scientists following Robin’s protocols; ripasudil still requires human clinical trials for dry AMD efficacy and safety.

scoreRationale.foundational: Established an open-source, end-to-end closed-loop multi-agent AI scientist blueprint spanning literature review, experimental design, and wet-lab data interpretation.
scoreRationale.ripple: Apache-2.0 release catalyzed widespread academic adoption of autonomous literature-and-data agents and directly spawned Edison Scientific’s Kosmos platform.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (May 2026) with multi-cycle wet-lab experimental validation across RPE cell assays and transcriptomic profiling.
scoreRationale.velocity: Synthesized 551 papers in 30 minutes (~200× researcher speedup) and compressed early-stage therapeutic repurposing discovery into weeks.
